Glycogen Storage Diseases
Glycogen storage diseases are caused by deﬁ ciencies of en-
zymes that regulate the synthesis or degradation of glycogen.
Glycogen, a polysaccharide composed of glucose units, is the 
main carbohydrate reserve in the body. Th is polysaccharide is 
assembled through a process of chain elongation and branch-
ing by the sequential addition of glucose units, achieved by 
glycogen synthetase and branching enzymes. Catabolism of the 
polysaccharide is achieved by the opposite process, through
phosphorylase and debranching enzymes (see Figure 26.9).
